Should I use my birth name or current name?

Are numerology results scientifically proven?

No. Numerology is a traditional symbolic system used for entertainment purposes only. It should not replace medical, legal, financial or psychological advice.

What are master numbers?

Master numbers are compound totals, commonly 11, 22 and 33, that some numerology traditions retain rather than immediately reducing. The methodology page explains exactly where this app retains them.

title: What Is Numerology? A Plain-English Guide
h1: What Is Numerology? A Plain-English Guide
description: What Is Numerology? A Plain-English Guide. Numerology is the study of the meaning of numbers in a person’s life, most often drawn fro
answer: Numerology is the study of the meaning of numbers in a person’s life, most often drawn from their birth date and full name.
sections:
What is numerology?

Numerology is the belief that numbers carry meaning and that the numbers in your birth date and name describe patterns in your character and life. It is a symbolic system for reflection and self-knowledge, not a science.

Where do the numbers come from?

Two sources: your date of birth gives your Life Path, Birthday and cycle numbers, and your full birth name gives your Expression, Soul Urge and Personality numbers. Each is reduced to a single digit, keeping the master numbers 11, 22 and 33.

What can it be used for?

People use numerology to reflect on strengths and blind spots, to think about timing through the personal-year cycle, and as a gentle prompt for decisions. It works best as a mirror for reflection rather than a prediction of fixed events.

title: How to Calculate Your Life Path Number
h1: How to Calculate Your Life Path Number
description: How to Calculate Your Life Path Number. To calculate your Life Path number, reduce your birth month, day and year to single digits
answer: To calculate your Life Path number, reduce your birth month, day and year to single digits, add the three results, then reduce again, keeping master numbers 11, 22 and 33.
sections:
The steps

  1. Reduce the month to one digit (e.g. December, 12, becomes 1+2=3).
  2. Reduce the day the same way.
  3. Reduce the year (1990 becomes 1+9+9+0=19, then 1+9=10, then 1+0=1).
  4. Add the three single digits and reduce once more.

A worked example

For 15 December 1990: month 12, 3; day 15, 6; year 1990, 1. Then 3+6+1=10, and 1+0=1, so the Life Path is 1.

Keeping master numbers

If any step lands on 11, 22 or 33, stop there and keep it as a master number rather than reducing further. These carry a higher-octave version of their single-digit root.

title: Why Numerology Calculators Disagree
description: Why Numerology Calculators Disagree. Numerology calculators disagree mainly because they use different letter systems (Pythagor
answer: Numerology calculators disagree mainly because they use different letter systems (Pythagorean or Chaldean), treat the letter Y differently, or reduce master numbers at different stages.
sections:
Different letter systems

The Pythagorean system assigns A to 1 through I to 9 and repeats, while the Chaldean system uses a different, sound-based set of values. A name number will often differ between the two.

The letter Y and master numbers

Calculators disagree on whether Y is a vowel or consonant, which changes Soul Urge and Personality results. They also differ on whether to keep or reduce 11, 22 and 33 mid-calculation.

Which is right?

Neither is objectively correct, because numerology is an interpretive system. What matters is using one consistent method. This site uses the Pythagorean system and keeps master numbers, and shows the working so you can follow every step.

title: Master Numbers 11, 22 and 33 in Numerology
description: Master Numbers 11, 22 and 33 in Numerology. Master numbers are 11, 22 and 33: double-digit numbers that are not reduced, because they
answer: Master numbers are 11, 22 and 33: double-digit numbers that are not reduced, because they carry a heightened, higher-octave version of the energy of 2, 4 and 6.
sections:
The three master numbers

Numerology keeps three numbers unreduced. 11 is the intuitive (a higher octave of 2), 22 is the master builder (a higher octave of 4), and 33 is the master teacher (a higher octave of 6).

Greater potential, greater pressure

Master numbers describe unusual potential, but also unusual intensity. An 11 can be deeply inspired yet prone to nervous tension; a 22 can build on a large scale yet feel great pressure; a 33 can serve selflessly yet risk taking on too much.

Reading a master number

If your number is a master number, read both it and its single-digit root (11 and 2, 22 and 4, 33 and 6). Many people grow into the full master expression gradually rather than living it constantly.

title: Birth Name vs Current Name in Numerology
h1: Birth Name vs Current Name in Numerology
description: Birth Name vs Current Name in Numerology. Numerology traditionally uses your full birth name for the core reading, because it reflec
answer: Numerology traditionally uses your full birth name for the core reading, because it reflects the identity you were given at the start, while a current or changed name is read separately.
sections:
Why the birth name is the core

Your full name at birth is treated as the blueprint, so the Expression, Soul Urge and Personality numbers are calculated from it. It represents the potential you were born with.

What a changed name shows

A married, chosen or shortened name can be calculated separately to show how you present and operate now. It is read as an overlay on the birth-name blueprint rather than a replacement.

Which to enter here

For the most traditional result, enter your full birth name. You can also run your current name to compare the two and see what each emphasises.

title: Life Path vs Expression Number: The Difference
description: Life Path vs Expression Number: The Difference. Your Life Path comes from your birth date and describes the road your life tends to follow
answer: Your Life Path comes from your birth date and describes the road your life tends to follow; your Expression comes from your full name and describes your natural talents and how you pursue that road.
sections:
Life Path: the road

The Life Path is drawn from your date of birth. It describes the overall direction, lessons and opportunities that recur across your life.

Expression: the toolkit

The Expression, or Destiny, number is drawn from the letters of your full birth name. It describes the abilities and style you bring to that journey.

Reading them together

They work as a pair: the Life Path is where you are heading, the Expression is what you have to work with. When they align, the path feels natural; when they differ, each adds a distinct layer.

title: Soul Urge Number Guide (Heart’s Desire)
description: Soul Urge Number Guide (Heart’s Desire). Your Soul Urge number, from the vowels of your full name, describes what you most deeply w
answer: Your Soul Urge number, from the vowels of your full name, describes what you most deeply want, your inner motivation beneath outward goals.
sections:
What the Soul Urge reveals

Also called the Heart’s Desire, the Soul Urge is calculated from the vowels in your full birth name. It points to the wants and values that quietly drive you.

How to calculate it

Keep only the vowels of your full name, give each its value 1 to 9, add them and reduce to a single digit, keeping master numbers. The letter Y is treated as a vowel when it is not next to another vowel.

Using it well

Read the Soul Urge alongside your Expression and Personality numbers. The Expression is what you can do, the Personality is how you appear, and the Soul Urge is what you truly want underneath.

title: Personality Number Guide: How Others First See You
description: Your Personality number, from the consonants of your name, shapes the first impression you make. How to calculate it and what each number means.
answer: Your Personality number comes from the consonants in your full birth name and describes the first impression you give, the outer layer others meet before they know you well.
sections:
What is a Personality number?

Your Personality number is calculated from the consonants of your full birth name. It describes the outward impression you make and the side of yourself you show the world before people know you well.

How to calculate your Personality number

  1. Write out your full birth name.
  2. Keep only the consonants.
  3. Give each letter its value from 1 to 9 (B=2, C=3, D=4, F=6, and so on).
  4. Add them and reduce to a single digit, keeping master numbers 11, 22 and 33.

Personality numbers 1 to 9 at a glance

  • 1: One makes you come across as capable, confident and self-directed, someone others instinctively look to.
  • 2: Two makes you seem gentle, approachable and warm, people feel safe opening up to you.
  • 3: Three makes you seem lively, charming and fun, a natural at first impressions.
  • 4: Four makes you seem grounded, capable and trustworthy, the steady one.
  • 5: Five makes you seem exciting, magnetic and full of energy.
  • 6: Six makes you seem warm, dependable and caring, the one people lean on.
  • 7: Seven makes you seem thoughtful, private and quietly wise.
  • 8: Eight makes you seem powerful, capable and authoritative.
  • 9: Nine makes you seem gracious, worldly and quietly noble.

title: Pinnacle Numbers Guide in Numerology
description: Pinnacle Numbers Guide in Numerology. Pinnacle numbers are four life-stage numbers, calculated from your birth date, that descri
answer: Pinnacle numbers are four life-stage numbers, calculated from your birth date, that describe the main themes and opportunities of each phase of your life.
sections:
The four pinnacles

Your life divides into four pinnacle periods. The first runs from birth to your mid-thirties, then three further phases of roughly nine years each. Each carries a number and a theme.

How they are found

The pinnacles come from combining the reduced month, day and year of your birth in set pairs. The first pinnacle length depends on your Life Path number, so everyone’s timing differs slightly.

Reading a pinnacle

A pinnacle describes the kind of growth a period invites, not a fixed event. Read each alongside the matching Challenge number, which names the lesson to work through in that same phase.

title: How to Calculate the Four Pinnacles
h1: How to Calculate the Four Pinnacles
description: How to Calculate the Four Pinnacles. To calculate the four Pinnacles, reduce your birth month, day and year, then add them in s
answer: To calculate the four Pinnacles, reduce your birth month, day and year, then add them in set pairs: month plus day, day plus year, the first two pinnacles added, and month plus year.
sections:
The four calculations

  1. First: reduced month + reduced day.
  2. Second: reduced day + reduced year.
  3. Third: first pinnacle + second pinnacle.
  4. Fourth: reduced month + reduced year.

Reduce each result to a single digit, keeping master numbers.

The timing of each

The first pinnacle lasts from birth until about age 36 minus your Life Path number. Each of the next three lasts roughly nine years, and the fourth runs for the rest of your life.

Let the tool do it

Our free chart calculates all four Pinnacles, their ages and the matching Challenge numbers for you, and shows the working so you can check every step.

title: Pinnacles vs Personal Year: What’s the Difference
description: Pinnacles vs Personal Year: What’s the Difference. Pinnacles describe long life-stage themes lasting years, while the Personal Year is a shor
answer: Pinnacles describe long life-stage themes lasting years, while the Personal Year is a shorter one-year cycle that repeats 1 to 9, so they work on different timescales.
sections:
Two different clocks

The Pinnacles are long chapters, each lasting roughly nine years or more. The Personal Year turns over every year, cycling from 1 to 9 and starting again.

How they interact

Think of the Pinnacle as the season and the Personal Year as the month within it. A given Personal Year 5 will feel different depending on which Pinnacle it falls inside.

Reading them together

Use the Pinnacle for the big theme of this stage of life and the Personal Year for the near-term focus. Together they give both the horizon and the next step.

title: Challenge Numbers Guide in Numerology
description: Challenge Numbers Guide in Numerology. Challenge numbers, calculated by subtracting parts of your birth date, name the main inner
answer: Challenge numbers, calculated by subtracting parts of your birth date, name the main inner lessons to work through in each stage of life, alongside the Pinnacles.
sections:
What a Challenge number is

Each Pinnacle period has a matching Challenge: a recurring difficulty or lesson that, once understood, becomes a strength. Challenge numbers are usually low (0 to 8).

How they are found

Challenges come from the difference between the reduced parts of your birth date, rather than their sum. A 0 challenge suggests a lesson that is yours to define freely.

Working with a Challenge

Read a Challenge as growth work, not a flaw. It names the tendency to watch during that life stage, and the quality you are being invited to develop.

title: Personal Year Guide: The Nine-Year Cycle
description: Personal Year Guide: The Nine-Year Cycle. A Personal Year is a one-year theme in a repeating nine-year cycle, found by adding your b
answer: A Personal Year is a one-year theme in a repeating nine-year cycle, found by adding your birth month and day to the current year and reducing to a single digit.
sections:
The nine-year cycle

Numerology runs in cycles of nine years. Each year carries a number from 1 (fresh starts) through 9 (completion), then the cycle begins again with a new 1.

How to find yours

Add your birth month and birth day to the current year, then reduce to a single digit. That number is your Personal Year, and it colours the whole year’s focus.

Using the cycle

Knowing your Personal Year helps with timing: a 1 year favours starting, a 4 year favours building, a 9 year favours completing and releasing. Our free chart calculates yours and links to a full page for each number.

title: Numerology Compatibility Guide

What is compared

The most common comparison is Life Path to Life Path, since that describes each person’s overall direction. Name numbers such as Expression and Soul Urge can be compared too for a fuller picture.

A "high" match suggests two people whose tendencies naturally support each other; a "lower" match simply means more differences to understand. Neither predicts success or failure.

Read compatibility as a conversation starter about strengths and differences, not a verdict. Our free tool compares two birth dates and links to a full page for every Life Path pairing.

title: Pythagorean Numerology Explained
description: Pythagorean Numerology Explained. Pythagorean numerology is the most common Western system, assigning the letters A to I the
answer: Pythagorean numerology is the most common Western system, assigning the letters A to I the values 1 to 9 and then repeating, and reducing all results to single digits or master numbers.
sections:
The letter values

In the Pythagorean system, A=1, B=2, up to I=9, then J starts again at 1, and so on to Z. Names are converted to numbers using this grid and reduced.

Why it is popular

It is straightforward, consistent and easy to follow, which is why most Western numerology sites, including this one, use it. The working is simple enough to check by hand.

Pythagorean vs Chaldean

The main alternative, the Chaldean system, uses different, sound-based values and never assigns 9 to a letter. The two often give different name numbers, so it is best to pick one and stay consistent.

title: Chaldean vs Pythagorean Numerology
description: Chaldean vs Pythagorean Numerology. Pythagorean numerology assigns letters values 1 to 9 in order, while Chaldean numerology u
answer: Pythagorean numerology assigns letters values 1 to 9 in order, while Chaldean numerology uses older, sound-based values from 1 to 8 and treats the name as it is actually used.
sections:
Pythagorean

The Pythagorean system maps A to I as 1 to 9 and repeats. It is the common Western method, simple to calculate, and the one used on this site.

Chaldean

The Chaldean system is older and sound-based. It assigns values 1 to 8 only (9 is treated as sacred and not given to a letter) and often uses the name a person actually goes by rather than the full birth name.

Which to use

Neither is objectively correct. Pythagorean is easier and more widely used; Chaldean is favoured by those who prefer its older roots. The key is consistency, since mixing the two gives meaningless results.

Challenges to watch

  • Can become domineering or stubborn

Your Life Path comes from your full date of birth: reduce the month, day and year to single digits (keeping master numbers 11, 22 and 33), then add those three results and reduce again. When that final total is 1, your Life Path is 1.

title: Name Numerology: What Your Name Reveals
h1: Name Numerology: What Your Name Reveals
description: Name numerology turns the letters of your name into numbers. Learn how the Expression, Soul Urge and Personality numbers are found from your name.
answer: Name numerology assigns each letter of your name a value from 1 to 9 and reduces the totals to reveal your Expression, Soul Urge and Personality numbers.
sections:
How name numerology works

In the Pythagorean system each letter A–Z carries a number from 1 to 9 (A=1, B=2 … I=9, then J=1 again, and so on). Adding the values of the letters in your full birth name, and reducing the totals, produces your name-based core numbers.

The three name numbers

  • Expression (Destiny), all the letters: your natural talents and life direction.
  • Soul Urge (Heart's Desire), the vowels: what you want most deeply.
  • Personality, the consonants: how others first experience you.

Which name should you use?

Traditionally the full name on your birth certificate is used for the core reading, because it reflects the identity you were given at the start. A current or changed name can be read separately to show how you present now.

title: Lucky Numbers in Numerology: How to Find Yours
description: How to find your lucky numbers in numerology from your birth date, what each number means, and a free tool that calculates them for you.
answer: Your lucky numbers in numerology come from your own chart, mainly your Life Path, Birthday and Personal Day numbers, rather than being chosen at random. This page explains how to find them and what they mean.
sections:
What are lucky numbers in numerology?

In numerology, your lucky numbers are not random. They are the core numbers of your own chart, the ones that repeat across your Life Path, Birthday and current cycle. Numbers that echo your chart are said to feel supportive to you, which is why they are personal rather than universal.

How to find your lucky numbers

  1. Life Path number, from your full date of birth, your single most important number.
  2. Birthday number, the day of the month you were born.
  3. Personal Day number, which changes daily and sets the tone for today.
  4. Where the same digit appears in more than one of these, it carries extra weight for you.

What your lucky numbers mean

Each number from 1 to 9 carries a theme, from the leadership of 1 to the completion of 9. Read the meaning of each on our Life Path meaning pages to see what your own lucky numbers point to.

Get your lucky numbers free

Our free numerology chart calculates your Life Path, Birthday and Personal Day numbers and shows your lucky numbers for today, with the arithmetic behind each so you can check it. The daily horoscope refreshes them each day.
